as the melanin content in skin within each population varies in a continuous manner.													1m

*	Explain Mendel's first law and second law of inheritance with events occurring in meiotic cell division.										(5 marks)
Alleles of each gene are located on a pair of homologous chromosomes and the 	two members of the homologous pair separate during anaphase I.				1m
Each gamete receives one member of the homologous pair and hence its allele.																	1m
Homologous pairs line up randomly along the equator of the cell during metaphase I.																1m
The members of each homologous pair then separate independently of the 	other pairs of chromosomes during anaphase I.									1m
The separation of alleles for one gene on a pair of homologous chromosomes is therefore independent of the separation of alleles for other genes located on the other chromosomes.													1m

*	The blood groups in humans (A, B, AB and O) are controlled by a single gene which has three alleles, IA, IB and i. i is recessive to both IA and IB. The son of Paul and Mary is of blood group B. Mary is of blood group A. Answer the questions below without using genetic diagrams.
a	What is the genotype of Mary? Explain your answer.			(3 marks)

b	A recessive allele which causes a genetic disease is located on the X chromosome. If Paul's mother has the disease and Mary is a carrier of the disease, what is the chance of the son of Paul and Mary having the disease? Explain your answer.									(3 marks)
a	Since Mary is of blood group A, she must possess at least one IA. The possible genotypes of her are IAIA or IAi. 									1m
Her son is of blood group B. It is not possible for him to possess an allele IA. The only allele that Mary can pass on to him is i.						1m
Thus, the genotype of Mary is IAi.								1m
b	As Paul's mother has the disease, she must have the disease allele on both X chromosomes. One of her X chromosomes passed on to Paul, so Paul has the disease. 													1m
Mary is a carrier of the disease. She must have a disease allele on one of her X chromosomes, and a normal allele on the other. 					1m
The son of Paul and Mary has only one X chromosome, which is from Mary. Therefore, there is a 50% chance for him to have the disease. 			1m
